hypothesis_a: Malmasi & Zampieri's MAZA system attributes its superior performance on complex word/lexical complexity prediction (SemEval-2016 Task 11) to the use of contextual features, indicating that surrounding context influences how complex a word is perceived to be.
hypothesis_b: Kuru's AI-KU system (SemEval-2016 Task 11), using word embeddings and substring features with an SVM classifier, found that context was uninfluential on performance, indicating a word's complexity can be predicted without relying on contextual information.

hypothesis_a: Le et al. (NII-HITACHI-UIT, TRECVID 2016) trained their video-text common-space embedding model by minimizing the L2 (Euclidean) distance between paired video and text representations.
hypothesis_b: Phan et al. (NII-Hitachi-UIT, TRECVID 2017) obtained better results by instead defining the similarity measure in the common embedding space as the dot product between representations, rather than minimizing L2 distance.

hypothesis_a: Dwibedi et al.'s temporal cycle-consistency learning approach learns video representations using only the video domain, via self-supervised temporal alignment of video frames, without incorporating text.
hypothesis_b: Ging et al.'s COOT (Cooperative Hierarchical Transformer) approach holds that effective video representation learning should align video and text in a cross-modal way, rather than modeling video alone.

hypothesis_a: Carton et al. (2020) expect that the human-annotated highlights/rationales in the FEVER fact-verification dataset are non-comprehensive, i.e. they do not mark all evidence relevant to a verdict.
hypothesis_b: DeYoung et al.'s ERASER benchmark (2020) characterizes/relies on FEVER's rationale annotations as comprehensive evidence spans when using them to evaluate rationalized NLP models, in contrast to Carton et al.'s characterization.

hypothesis_a: Bhatia et al. (2015) show that using an external RST discourse parser to derive a document's discourse structure improves document-level sentiment analysis.
hypothesis_b: Ji & Smith (2017) point out limitations of relying on external discourse parsers for tasks like text categorization, arguing discourse structure should instead be modeled directly rather than depending on an off-the-shelf parser.
